explanation: Heating lead nitrate crystals decomposes them into lead(II) oxide, releasing brown fumes of nitrogen dioxide and oxygen gas.

beaker_view.initial_appearance: White, colourless crystals of lead nitrate.
beaker_view.final_appearance: A yellow powdery residue of lead oxide.

thermal.visual_cue: Needs continuous heating, and gives off brown fumes as it decomposes.

beaker_view.observation: As the white crystals are heated, they hiss and release brown fumes, leaving behind a yellow powder.
